title: attachments-catalog — case shape (v0.1)
description: Pins one byte-level case for the MYC1 attachments catalog (vault.attachments). Reference impl: protocol/src/attachments_catalog.rs (main myne repository); spec contract: docs/spec/protocol.md §9.10 + §5.2 + §3.4. Four case kinds: 'encrypt' (encoder byte output over canonical JSON, incl. empty {}), 'decrypt_ok' (round-trip), 'decrypt_aead_fail' (non-distinguishing AEAD failure per §6.4 / §9.10.4; read_or_empty falls to {} on these), 'aad_construction' (aad_attachments_catalog canonical bytes). KEK = DeriveSubkey(root_key,'attachments-catalog-key'). Inner plaintext maps lowercase-hex attachment-id -> {content_type,created_at,filename,scope,size} with keys lexicographically sorted. `scope` is optional and emitted only for the value `chat` (myne-md/myne#913); it sits between `filename` and `size`, its absence means the attachment library, and an unknown value decodes as the library rather than failing the catalog.

oneOf.title: encrypt — pin the encoder's MYC1 byte output

input_root_key_hex.description: 32-byte root_key (hex). The encoder derives the catalog KEK via DeriveSubkey(root_key, AttachmentsCatalogKey).

input_plaintext_canonical_utf8_hex.description: Canonical-JSON inner plaintext bytes (hex). Empty catalog = {} = 7b7d.

informational_catalog_key_hex.description: 32-byte derived KEK (hex). Informational — verified implicitly via expected_catalog_blob_hex.

expected_catalog_blob_hex.description: Full encoder output (34-byte header + ciphertext + 32-byte CTX tag), hex.

oneOf.title: decrypt_ok — pin the decoder's successful round-trip

expected_plaintext_canonical_utf8_hex.description: The canonical-JSON re-encode of the decoded catalog (hex). For ordinary round-trip cases this equals the sealed inner plaintext; for forward-compat tolerance cases (sealed plaintext carries unknown additive per-entry fields, spec §9.10.2) it is the canonical form WITHOUT the unknown fields — comparison is structural, the sealed bytes then live in informational_sealed_plaintext_utf8_hex.

informational_sealed_plaintext_utf8_hex.description: Optional. The verbatim inner plaintext sealed into input_blob_hex, when it differs from expected_plaintext_canonical_utf8_hex (forward-compat tolerance cases only). Informational — lets reviewers inspect the unknown-field payload without an AEAD implementation.

oneOf.title: decrypt_aead_fail — pin the non-distinguishing failure surface

expected_kind.description: The decoder MUST report a non-distinguishing AEAD failure (Rust: CatalogBlobError::CannotDecrypt); read_or_empty collapses it to the empty catalog {}.

oneOf.title: parse_fail — pin a distinguishable structural or inner-plaintext reject

input_blob_hex.description: A malformed blob (hex, empty allowed). Six of the seven rejects fire BEFORE the AEAD stage; plaintext_parse_failed fires AFTER a successful AEAD open, on the canonical-JSON parse.

input_root_key_hex.description: 32-byte root_key (hex). REAL key, deliberately: header bytes are not AAD-bound, so a port that skips a structural check decrypts the tampered blob successfully and returns Ok — which the runner catches. The plaintext_parse_failed case additionally needs the key to get past AEAD.

expected_error.description: The specific reject the decoder MUST surface (Rust reference: CatalogBlobError::{HeaderTooShort, MagicMismatch, ProtocolVersionMismatch, ReservedByteNonZero, CiphertextLenOverflow, CiphertextTruncated, PlaintextParseFailed}). Intentionally distinguishable for observability — callers then fall back to the empty catalog per §9.10.4.
